description:
Hello Earthlings!!

We're interested in space, engineering, programming, and scientific research. For this challenge, we're exploring how health monitoring software can help astronauts better understand and act on changes in their health during long-duration space missions.
summary: Dr. Cosmos is a direct response to the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. It is a single page web dashboard which is modular, responsive, and card-based with light and dark mode capabilities that brings together health tools and verified reference materials in an easily accessible way. To reduce visual clutter and cognitive load during high-stress spaceflight operations, the software organizes medical and operational data using embedded iframe views, a sticky navigation bar, and an interactive sources section. This is critical for outerspace,  Earth isolated missions: astronauts will be able to proactively monitor their health and make rapid, autonomous medical decisions when real-time communication with Earth is not feasible. This centralized, easy-to-use monitoring suite is a must have.
details: Built for the Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions challenge, Dr Cosmos is a responsive, single-page web dashboard developed using HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript that consolidates modular health utilities via embedded iframes alongside an interactive, toggleable sources section. Creatively reimagining dense aerospace telemetry as a calm, cohesive workspace, the software reduces cognitive load and enables rapid, clutter-free switching between vital medical tools and verified references. In designing the suite, our team prioritized usability under high-stress conditions, cross-device responsiveness from consoles to tablets, offline reliability through dependency-free web standards, and environmental ergonomics via full light and dark mode compatibility for shifting cabin lighting. Ultimately, this centralized health suite empowers astronauts on isolated deep-space missions to proactively monitor their well-being and make informed, autonomous medical decisions when real-time communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable.
